P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, but under CEMAC exchange control (Regulation 02/18/CEMAC/UMAC/CM). Service-export receipts must be collected and repatriated by the exporter through its domiciliary bank via the BEAC (art. 70). Service transactions of FCFA 5m or more must be domiciled with a CEMAC credit institution (art. 68) and backed by a contract, purchase order or invoice (art. 69). Foreign currency received by banks is surrendered to the BEAC.

sources.quote: Article 70. Les recettes d'exportation des services sont recouvrées et rapatriées par I'exportateur à travers sa banque domiciliataire par I'entremise de la Banque Centrale.

sources.quote: Article 68. Les transactions avec I'extérieur liées aux services d'un montant égal ou supérieur à 5 millions de Francs CFA sont domiciliées auprès d'un établissement de crédit de la CEMAC.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: No. Opening a foreign-currency account within CEMAC for a resident is not authorised (art. 43). Only resident legal persons may be authorised by the BEAC. Resident individuals' accounts abroad must be declared to the BEAC (art. 42).

sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 43
sources.quote: Article 43. L'ouverture d'un compte en devises dans la CEMAC au profit d'un résident n'est pas autorisée.

sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 42
sources.quote: Article 42. Les comptes des personnes physiques résidentes ouverts à l'étranger sont déclarés à la Banque Centrale.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest: an individual enterprise (entreprise individuelle). It needs no minimum capital, has unlimited personal liability, and is taxed under personal income tax. It is registered through the ANPI-Gabon one-stop shop, which issues the RCCM and NIF together. In July 2024 ANPI announced a planned cut of the formalisation fee for individual enterprises from FCFA 85,000 to 50,000; whether it was adopted was not confirmed.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The NIF (Numéro d'Identification Fiscale), issued by the DGI. It is mandatory for businesses and for individuals with tax obligations; its format is 7 digits plus a letter. Businesses registering at ANPI receive it with the RCCM.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Personal income tax (IRPP) applies to people habitually resident in Gabon or resident for at least 183 days in the year (CGI art. 74). Small businesses with turnover under FCFA 30m pay the Impôt Synthétique Libératoire (ISL); those with FCFA 30–60m are under the simplified regime (RSI). These taxpayers, explicitly including online sellers, are handled by the small-business tax centres (CIPEP) and are being moved onto the e-Tax platform. How foreign-source income is taxed was not established.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Per the 2026 Kreston/Exco tax booklet, the standard VAT rate is 18% (reduced rates 10%, 5%, 0%; CGI art. 221), and the registration threshold is FCFA 60m turnover (FCFA 500m for forestry). One guide gives an 80m threshold but marks it unconfirmed. Treatment of exported digital services was not established.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Law 025/2023 of 12 July 2023 (JO n°218 bis, 15 July 2023) rewrote Law 001/2011 on personal data protection. The regulator is the APDPVP (successor to the CNPDCP). Automated processing must be declared to the APDPVP (art. 78); simplified norms allow simplified declarations or exemptions. Fines run from FCFA 1m to 100m (art. 204).

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Law 025/2021 of 28 Dec 2021 on electronic transactions (JO n°145, 1 Jan 2022) governs e-commerce. Sellers must give easy, permanent access to their identification details (art. 31) and state prices clearly, including whether taxes and fees are included (art. 32). Consumers may withdraw from a distance contract within 14 calendar days without giving reasons, bearing only direct return costs (art. 57); for services the period runs from the conclusion of the contract. Gabon had no general consumer-protection law in 2023; a 2022 bill existed.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
